question: Under what condition can one whose mind is fixed on that remain uncut even when being cut?
premises: Cutting is being applied to one who is being cut.
A mind fixed on that remains directed to that object.
Absence of severance holds only when the mind is so directed.
inference: One whose mind is fixed on that is not severed by the act of cutting, just as stated.
uncertainties: Extent of the scope of 'that' remains context-dependent.
plain_english: Just as one whose mind is fixed on that is not cut when being cut, so too no severance occurs in that state.
